error.signature: AI tells a Saudi Arabia tourist e-visa holder or Hajj pilgrim they can open a normal bank account with just a passport

verdict.summary: SAMA's Rulebook sets different, restricted bank-account rules by visa type in Saudi Arabia. Only Iqama (residence permit) holders get a normal account. Tourists/visitors hold a Ministry of Interior Visitor ID and get an account that closes when their permit expires and cannot receive a checkbook. Temporary work-visa holders (first 90 days) are limited to an ATM card and transfers up to SAR 10,000 per transaction. Foreign pilgrims holding only a Hajj identification card are not allowed to open a bank account at all.

dead_ends.action: Tell a tourist e-visa holder or short-term visitor that a passport alone lets them open a regular Saudi bank account the way an Iqama (residency) holder can
dead_ends.why_fails: SAMA's Rulebook classifies visitor/tourist accounts under a separate, restricted category: valid only through the visa/Visitor ID's expiry (closing immediately for single-entry visas), with no checkbook, and treated as high-risk. It is not the same account product a resident opens with an Iqama.
dead_ends.condition: Tourist e-visa or short-term visitor without an Iqama
dead_ends.common_misconception: That any valid Saudi entry visa is enough to open a full bank account, the same as a resident.

dead_ends.action: Assume a foreign Hajj pilgrim can open a bank account in Saudi Arabia using their Hajj identification card
dead_ends.why_fails: SAMA's Rulebook explicitly lists foreign pilgrims holding only a Hajj identification card among the prohibited-account categories: banks are not allowed to open accounts for them on that basis at all.
dead_ends.condition: Hajj pilgrim without a separate residency or visitor account basis

dead_ends.action: Tell a new temporary work-visa holder they get full banking services (checkbook, credit card, unlimited transfers) as soon as the account is opened
dead_ends.why_fails: During the first 90 days before the Iqama is issued, SAMA restricts the account to an ATM card and transfers capped at SAR 10,000 per transaction; no checkbooks or credit cards are permitted, and the account freezes if the Iqama is not submitted within three months.
dead_ends.condition: First 90 days on a temporary work visa, before Iqama issuance

workarounds.action: Wait until Iqama (residence permit) issuance to open a full-service account; in the interim, use the restricted temporary-work-visa account (ATM card + capped transfers) that SAMA permits during the first 90 days
workarounds.how: Provide the employer's official request, original passport with work visa, and sign the account-opening agreement in person; submit the Iqama within three months to avoid the account freezing.

workarounds.action: For a genuine tourist/visitor need (e.g. a long multiple-entry visit visa), apply for the restricted visitor account with a Ministry of Interior Visitor ID, a stated purpose of visit, and expect only a MADA-network ATM card and no checkbook
workarounds.how: Multiple-entry visit visas can get a 6-month renewable account; single-entry visas get an account that closes when the visa expires.
workarounds.condition: Visit-visa holder (business, scientific, professional, or government visit)

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers whether Saudi Arabia issues a tourist e-visa at all; this one covers the separate, much more restricted bank-account rules that apply once someone is in the country on that visa.
